deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, Dec. 1983): Grothendieck is studying systems (arrangements) of pseudo-lines in the projective plane. He uses a combinatorial cellular structure, which he calls a 'grapho-variété', on a space Gamma^n(E) of such configurations or on the arrangement itself. To each vertex D he attaches a local polygon Pol^(D). By the previous page, the vertices of Pol^(D) are the edges issuing from D. For a specialization D -> D' he considers 'specialization morphisms' Pol^(D) -> Pol^(D').

The previous page asked whether these morphisms can be recovered from the cellular structure. Its answer was yes, given three things: (a) cyclic order, (b) the effect on one orientation, and (c) the image of one marked vertex (D,alpha), which goes to the antipode of (D',alpha). It ended with an observation: for a 2-cell with three vertices of index 2, the comparison maps between local polygons form a local system on the underlying surface.

This page has two parts.

(1) He notes that in the present case these two facts (or questions) are not evident. The morphisms Pol^(D) -> Pol^(D') have 'singular properties'. One should examine thoroughly the relations and specializations involving a singular Delta.

(2) Entry of 24.12, the decisive reformulation. The 'right' object is Pol^(D) or, rather, its dual polygon Pol(D). Passing to the dual amounts to taking the dual map (carte duale) of the cell map considered, and the dual map is the more natural one. Pol(D) is to be visualized in two equivalent ways:
- as the boundary of a small tubular (regular) neighbourhood of D;
- as the boundary of a disc Delta(D), the dual cell of D.

The global map is then recovered by gluing the discs Delta(D) in a natural way. The procedure is as follows:
- take certain distinguished edges on the boundary of each Delta(D);
- fold or contract them, producing a disc Delta'(D);
- in Delta'(D) the previously adjacent (contracted) edges appear as segments running from the boundary to the interior.

If one keeps the trace of the pseudo-lines (drawn in red) inside Delta'(D), one finds double points. The small figure shows this near the boundary: a circle labelled 1..10 with red and green inward segments. So the dual disc carries a local picture of the pseudo-lines through D, resolved into simple crossings.

The large figure shows a star-like arrangement of orange pseudo-lines in a disc, with boundary points numbered 1..11, i.e. a model of the projective plane, with blue marks at the boundary. In modern terms the page is moving from the arrangement or cell complex to its dual cell decomposition. In that decomposition each vertex D becomes a polygon Delta(D) whose boundary records the strands through D. For a multiple point of k strands this is a 2k-gon, inside which a simple local resolution appears as a pattern of double points. This is close to the now-standard duality between pseudo-line arrangements and tilings of zonogons by centrally symmetric polygons (rhombic tilings for simple arrangements).

The purpose is to obtain a natural, intrinsic description of the specialization morphisms and of the local structure of the configuration space of pseudo-line systems.
errors: No clear mathematical error is checkable; the page is a heuristic reformulation.
The precise meaning of D (multiple point of an arrangement vs. vertex of a configuration complex Gamma^n(E)) cannot be fixed from this page, so the reconstruction is partly conjectural.
The 'folding' construction of Delta'(D) is described only qualitatively; how the discs are glued is not specified ('que je viens de m'expliquer').

ideas.what: Replacing the local link polygon Pol^(D) by its dual Pol(D), seen as the boundary of a regular/tubular neighbourhood of D or of the dual disc Delta(D).
ideas.modern_name: dual cell decomposition / link vs. dual cell of a vertex in a cellular surface
ideas.where_published: Maps and duality are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in the context of dessins/cartes, but not for pseudo-lines

ideas.what: Recovering the global map by gluing the dual discs Delta(D), each containing the local trace of the pseudo-lines, with double points appearing inside.
ideas.modern_name: duality between pseudo-line arrangements and zonogon (rhombic / centrally-symmetric) tilings; local resolution of a multiple point as a rhombic tiling of a 2k-gon
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for the flip graph; Bohne–Dress (c. 1989-92) and Felsner–Ziegler/Elnitsky (1990s) for the tiling duality; Manin–Schechtman (1986) for higher Bruhat orders B(n,2)

ideas.what: Specialization morphisms between local polygons Pol^(D) -> Pol^(D') in a stratified space of pseudo-line configurations, with attention to 'singular' Delta.
ideas.modern_name: stratification of the space of pseudo-line arrangements / oriented-matroid strata, face poset maps

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently arrives (Dec. 1983) at the idea that the natural object is the dual map of a pseudo-line arrangement. In it each vertex becomes a polygon whose interior carries the resolved local crossings, which is essentially the zonotopal/rhombic tiling duality later made standard (Bohne–Dress, Felsner, Elnitsky), and he links it to specialization maps between local polygons. This predates or is contemporaneous with Manin–Schechtman's higher Bruhat orders, and the connection to his 'grapho-variété' and 'carte' viewpoint (maps on surfaces, as in the Esquisse) is not in the literature.
missed.quote: c'est la carte duale qui est la plus naturelle ... la carte qui nous intéresse peut être considérée comme obtenue en recollant les disques Δ(D)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority/independent discovery of the arrangement–tiling duality in the context of Grothendieck's combinatorial-topological program; possibly a different, map-theoretic (dessin-like) viewpoint on spaces of pseudo-line arrangements.

missed.claim: He flags that specialization morphisms Pol^(D) -> Pol^(D') have 'singular' behaviour and that relations and specializations involving a singular Delta must be examined; this is left open.
missed.quote: Il faudrait examiner à fond les relations et spécialisations avec un Δ singulier
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Concerns the local structure of the stratified configuration space of pseudo-line arrangements; such stratifications are notoriously wild (Mnëv universality), so his combinatorial approach to them is of some interest, though it is only sketched.

deep.surprise_reason: A plausible independent arrival at the dual (tiling) viewpoint on pseudo-line arrangements within Grothendieck's own framework of maps and cell complexes. The page is heuristic, largely illegible in detail, and the underlying duality is now standard.
transcription_corrections: 'les deuxanneaux [?] Pol^∧(D) → Pol^∧(D')' should probably read 'les deux morphismes Pol^∧(D) → Pol^∧(D')'; 'anneaux' does not fit the context.
'carte duale' has 'duale' underlined in the image.
On the right column the quoted boundary edges are written in quotation marks, something like 'les "arêtes ..."' (possibly 'cassées' or 'césures'); illegible.
The parenthetical '(nouvelle option [?]!)' may read '(nouvelle astuce!)'; uncertain.

The large figure has boundary points numbered 1–11, with blue marks at the boundary arcs; the small figure has boundary labels 1–10 with red and green inward segments, illustrating Δ'(D) near its boundary.
